title: Inbox: a text size setting
intent: The Inbox draws its text at one size today, and nobody can change it. This plan adds a Text size row to Settings with 12, 13, 14 and 15, where 14 stays the default. A pick changes the whole window at once and is saved for the next time.

AG-TS.label: Project notes after the change: the Text size setting
quote: a segmented 12 / 13 / 14 / 15 control in Appearance, the Theme control's style, applied at once with no reload
I could also go to 13 or 15 or even 12

AG-RAMP.label: Project notes after the change: how the sizes scale
quote: so the whole ramp (rows, subjects, the sidebar, message bodies, question cards, Settings, timestamps, chips, badges) keeps its relative steps
Phone controls' 16 px take `--ib-fs-16-in = max(16px, …)`, so iOS never zooms

AG-SAME.label: Project notes after the change: what stays
quote: at 14 each size is exactly today's (a screenshot at 14 is byte-identical to the window before the setting)
Row and control heights keep today's pitch, so phones keep 44 px targets

quote: adopted from the first settings read like the theme (never over a pick made on the page first)
the `plannotator-inbox-text-size` cookie keeps the last size this browser showed, so a reload paints at it before the read answers

overview.text: One setting sizes the whole Inbox: 12, 13, 14 or 15, and 14 is the default.
Settings gets a Text size row. A pick shows at once, with no reload.
The server saves the size in config.json and refuses any other value.
At 14 the window draws exactly as it does today.
Is 14 the right default? Try each size, then decide.

parts.title: What a person sees today
body: Settings, General, Appearance holds one row today: Theme. Nothing there changes how large the text is.
Someone who finds the Inbox too small or too large has no way to change it. The text size is fixed in the stylesheet.

figure.caption: The Appearance group before the change: Theme only.

parts.title: What the plan adds
body: A second row, Text size, with a button for each size: 12, 13, 14 and 15. It looks like the Theme control above it.
The size applies to the whole Inbox, at once, with no reload. Use the buttons on the right to compare.

sections.title: How the Inbox sizes its text today

parts.title: One number already drives every size
body: Every text size in the stylesheet already comes from one number, `--ib-type`. Today it is 14.
A hidden switch can take it down to 13, so the owner could compare. No person can reach that switch from the window.

figure.title: The type knob at the base commit
text: /* Type (--ib-soft-type): one knob. --ib-type is the window's base size in px, 14 (today's) or 13 when on, and
every size the window sets is N px * --ib-type / 14 (exact: 14 px is 13 px on, N px off), and ui's drawing inside it through its type scale (below); a size never goes under
12 px, and sizes already under 12 px are left as they are. Phone inputs keep 16 px (iOS zooms under it).
Used as font-size: var(--ib-fs-N, Npx); off, each is exactly today's N px. Row and control heights keep
today's pitch, so phones keep their 44 px targets. */
figure.caption: The marked lines go. In their place, the knob reads the person's setting.

parts.title: What follows that number
body: The list rows, subjects, the sidebar, message bodies, question cards, Settings, and the small labels all scale from it. Their steps stay the same relative to each other.
Nothing shrinks past its floor: no text goes under 11 px, and phone controls stay at 16 px, so iOS does not zoom.

figure.title: What scales, and what never shrinks

rows.note: never under 16 px, so iOS never zooms

figure.caption: Every size moves together, above its floor.

sections.title: The setting, from the screen to the page

parts.title: The Text size row
body: The row draws its buttons from one shared list of sizes, so the screen and the server agree. A pick calls `chooseTextSize`.
Its description changes with the pick: at 14 it says this is the default.

figure.title: The new row in Settings
text: {textSize === 14 ? 'The default. Applies to the whole Inbox.' : 'Applies to the whole Inbox; 14 is the default.'}
figure.caption: One button per size in the shared list. A pick shows and saves it.

parts.title: Shown at once
body: The page puts the size on the document as one style value, `--inbox-text-size`. The stylesheet reads it, so every size changes in the same frame.
At 14 the value is removed, not set. The stylesheet then falls back to its own 14, which is why 14 draws exactly as today.

figure.title: Putting the size on the page
text: * Put `size` on the document. At 14 the property is removed, so the window
* draws from inbox.css's own default, exactly as before the setting existed.
// A page with no cookies still shows the size; it is only not remembered here.
figure.caption: At 14 the value is removed; at any other size it is set.

parts.title: What happens on a pick
body: Step through one pick of 15. The screen changes first, then the page and the server both remember it.
A cookie lets the next visit paint at 15 at once. config.json is the size every browser on this computer starts from.

parts.title: Only the listed sizes are saved
body: The settings route takes `text_size` and saves it in config.json as `inboxTextSize`. Anything but 12, 13, 14 or 15 is refused with 422, and nothing is saved.
Try a value on the right to see the answer.

then.caption: 15 is in the list, so it is saved.
16 is not in the list: refused, nothing saved.
Only whole sizes are kept: 13.5 is refused.
A number written as text is refused too.

parts.title: The check, in the code
body: One function checks the value, saves it, and reads the file back. If the file did not change, the route says so instead of claiming success.

figure.title: Checking and saving the size
text: const saveTextSize = (input: unknown, validateOnly = false): InboxTextSize => {
if (!isInboxTextSize(input)) throw new InboxError("validation_error", "text_size: 12, 13, 14 or 15.", { field: "text_size" });
if (loadConfig().inboxTextSize !== input) throw new InboxError("config_not_saved", "config.json could not be written; nothing changed.");
figure.caption: Refuse anything else, save, then confirm the file really changed.

parts.title: Which size a new visit shows
body: On the next visit, the cookie paints the page before the first render. Then the first settings read answers with config.json's size, and that wins.
One exception: a size the person picked on this page before that read answered is never undone by it.

figure.title: A new visit, in order
figure.caption: The cookie avoids a jump; config.json has the last word.

parts.title: Today's window, untouched
body: Nobody has to do anything. Until someone picks a size, the window is 14, and at 14 every size is exactly today's.
Row and control heights do not change at any size, so phones keep their 44 px targets.

figure.title: The sizes
figure.caption: 14 is the default, and today's window.

parts.title: Is 14 the right default?
body: The setting exists so the sizes can be tried for real before the default is chosen. The plan keeps 14 for now.
Before changing it, use each size for a while on a real Inbox, then decide.

figure.title: Deciding the default
figure.caption: The default is the one thing left to decide.
